page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-4GB is a virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture and a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 30 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server type.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores also rank in the top 25%. However, multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations show clear performance tradeoffs. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation, image processing, and Passmark database operations all fall into the bottom 25% performance tier, reflecting the constraints of the shared CPU allocation and modest memory bandwidth.

Positioned within the Starter family, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores or massive memory arrays. The qualitative resource density is tailored for lightweight, single-threaded tasks. Appropriate workloads include basic static web serving, Redis caching operations, and lightweight text processing. It is less suitable for multi-threaded compilation, database hosting, or complex image processing due to the observed multi-core performance limitations.
